title: Dual Data-centric Separation with Circular Mixup for Noise-resistant Time Series Learning

problem.claim: Noise-resistant time series learning under real-world label noise.

gap.claim: Noise-resistant time series learning is described as underexplored despite being realistic.

contributions.claim: DREAM uses dual data-centric views to explore noisy data and reduce overfitting.
DREAM infers pseudo labels and pseudo margins from an affinity graph, and uses simulated mislabeled data to separate clean and noisy samples.
DREAM applies circular Mixup in embedding space and discrepancy-aware consistency learning to learn robust representations from separated samples.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DREAM as a novel data-centric approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on a wide range of publicly accessible datasets are reported to reveal DREAM's effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: DNNs have made extensive progress in time series learning.
Real-world label noise can degrade performance, motivating noise-resistant time series learning.
DREAM exploits noisy data through dual data-centric views, pseudo-label affinity analysis, and simulated-noise-based sample separation.
Circular Mixup and discrepancy-aware consistency learning are used to improve representations across separated samples.
The authors report effectiveness on a wide range of publicly accessible datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, noise rates, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational requirements, or ablation results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness.
